To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified a set of miRNAs associated to prognosis in triple-negative tumours, that we have identified miRNAs that are specifically expressed in different intrinsic molecular subgroups and we have shown how these miRNAs are influenced by DNA copy number aberrations and how they contribute to the activation of oncogenetic pathways.

1) we identify miRNAs associated to clinical outcomes in triple-negative tumours, 2) we identify miRNA expression profiles associated with molecular subtypes and 3) we show how miRNA expression levels are influenced by DNA copy number and how they contribute to the transcriptional profile of basal-like tumours
we identified miRNAs associated to clinical and molecular phenotypic traits of triple-negative breast tumours, and that we shed light on the pathways controlled by these miRNAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel miRNA biomarkers and the elucidation of the pathways and mechanisms they control in triple-negative tumours.
identifying miRNAs associated to clinical and biological phenotypes in triple-negative tumours.
the identification of novel miRNA biomarkers for breast cancer prognosis and the analysis of the pathways that they control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the miRNAs that are associated with prognosis and/or with the intrinsic molecular subtype of breast tumours are involved in a variety of biological pathways and are influenced by DNA genomic alterations.

our results provide a conceptual framework, integrative methods, and system-level results, that contribute to elucidate the roles of miRNAs in breast cancer, and particularly in the triple negative subtype.
miRNAs play a key role in triple-negative tumours, which may be used for prognosis and as therapeutic targets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a number of miRNAs with prognostic potential in triple-negative breast cancer and have provided a comprehensive view of how these miRNAs influence the molecular and clinical phenotype of this disease.
we have shown that the miRNAs that are differentially expressed between triple-negative tumour types are involved in the regulation of pathways that are associated with tumour progression.
we have identified a group of miRNAs that are associated with clinical outcomes in breast cancer, and that these are likely to play an important role in the regulation of tumour invasion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a subset of miRNAs are associated with clinical outcome in triple-negative and ER-negative breast cancers.
miRNAs can be used as prognostic and predictive biomarkers, and as potential therapeutic targets, in triple-negative tumours.
the expression levels of miRNAs are associated with clinical and biological characteristics of breast cancers and can be used as prognostic markers and potential therapeutic targets.
